sanskrit_verse: आयुधान्य आयुधीयानां वाह्यादीन् वाह्यजीविनाम्‌ । वेश्यास्त्रीणामलंकारं वाद्यातोद्यानि तद्विदाम्‌ ॥
transliteration: āyudhāny āyudhīyānāṃ vāhyādīn vāhyajīvinām | veśyāstrīṇām alaṃkāraṃ vādyātodyāni tadvidām ||
sph_interpretive_translation: The instruments of war belong to warriors; conveyances and draft animals belong to those who operate them; ornaments belong to courtesans; musical instruments belong to those skilled in music.
jurisprudential_principles: Functional possession rooted in skill and usage
executable_legal_axioms: IF entity E demonstrates operational mastery over instrument I, THEN E holds lawful claim to I.
IF entity E utilizes resource R for sustenance S, THEN E's ownership of R is valid within context S.
IF entity E performs skill K using tool T, THEN E retains custodianship of T relative to K.
IF disalignment occurs in instrumental possession, THEN restoration process initiates reconnection between user and tool.
IF ownership dispute arises, adjudicate based on active usage pattern, not historical claim.
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, disputes involving proprietary claims shall be resolved by evaluating the functional relationship between individual and asset, prioritizing living engagement over abstract entitlement. Responsibility thresholds are determined by demonstrated instrumental mastery and existential reliance.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes causality through observed instrumental use; anupūrvaśaḥ traces ownership back to conscious engagement sequence; proportional responsibility aligns with actual usage depth; non-punitive reality rule ensures misaligned assets are returned to rightful users without infliction of harm.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Reconnect individual with instrument of livelihood
Validate experiential mastery through practical assessment
Restore displaced ownership through witnessed realignment
Facilitate completion of interrupted economic or creative flow
Ensure no loss of dignity during restitution process
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands declared: Dharma prevails through rightful instrumental alignment, reality remains free from punitive distortion, and consciousness alone serves as the ultimate arbiter of justice.
